nota.t: Numbers are written with numbers (eg 45) and words (forty five).
45 = 40 + 5 · digit 4 is worth 40, digit 5 is worth 5
Patterns can count one-one, two-two, five-five or ten-ten, forward or backward.

glosari: The symbols 0 to 9 that make up the numbers.
Digit position, either sa or tens.
A sequence of numbers that follow certain rules.

topik.nama: Add and Subtract in the Neighborhood of 100

nota.t: Subtract means to take out or find a difference. The − symbol. > 28 − 5 = 23
Write the numbers in the tens and ones columns. Start with the sa column. If the result of sa is greater than 9, regroup to the tens column.
Check the subtraction answer by adding: 28 − 5 = 23 because 23 + 5 = 28.

glosari: The answer to the subtraction operation.
Converts 10 sa to 1 ten, or vice versa.

nota.t: An object can be divided into parts of equal size.
Portions must be equally large. If it's not the same size, it's not a half or a quarter.

glosari: The number above the fraction line.
The number below the fractional line; the same number of parts.

nota.t: Coins: 5 sen, 10 sen, 20 sen, 50 sen · Banknote: RM1, RM5, RM10
100 sen = RM1 · 2 pieces 50 sen = RM1 · 2 pieces RM5 = RM10
Balance = money paid − price of goods.

glosari: A small unit of money; 100 cents is equivalent to RM1.

nota.t: There are 7 days in a week. A year has 12 months.
The short hand indicates the hour. The long hand shows the minutes.
Long hand at 12 → o'clock exactly · Long hand at 6 → half hour

glosari: Table of days and months of the year.

nota.t: We can compare: long – short, tall – short, heavy – light, much – little.
We can measure with a paper clip, span, footprint, marble or cup. More units mean longer, heavier or more content.

glosari: The distance between the tip of the thumb and the tip of the little finger when the hand is open.
The amount of liquid in a container.

nota.t: cube 🎲 · cuboid 📦 · cylinder 🥫 · cone 🍦 · sphere ⚽ · pyramid 🔺
3D shapes have surfaces; 2D shapes are flat shapes.

glosari: The outside of a 3D shape, either flat or curved.
The meeting point of two sides.

nota.t: Pictographs use pictures to represent data. Each picture represents one object.

t: Count the pictures for each item.

glosari: Charts that use pictures to represent data.
